title: Hosting LLM on Kubernetes
subtitle: Self-hosted Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct LLM on Kubernetes cluster managed via Argo CD GitOps, secured with Cloudflare Tunnels & Traefik Ingress, orchestrated by LiteLLM Gateway, NextChat UI, Headlamp dashboard, Langfuse tracing, and Netdata telemetry.

overview.summary: An enterprise-grade, privacy-first LLM hosting platform running entirely on Kubernetes and automated via GitOps (Local PC -> GitHub -> Argo CD). External users route through Cloudflare Portal DNS & edge security into an in-cluster Cloudflared Tunnel, which passes traffic to Traefik Ingress Controller. The parent Kubernetes cluster encapsulates all microservices and inference engines: serving the high-performance Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct model behind an intelligent LiteLLM proxy, fronted by NextChat UI, managed visually via Headlamp, tracked comprehensively by Langfuse for prompt/token telemetry, and monitored in real time via Netdata.
overview.problemStatement: Commercial LLM APIs introduce recurring per-token expenses, vendor lock-in, data privacy hazards, and opaque latency spikes. Deploying raw self-hosted models without unified ingress, zero-trust perimeter security, GitOps automation, session tracking, and hardware telemetry leads to unmanaged token exhaustion, configuration drift, exposed firewall ports, and operational blind spots.
corePrinciples: Declarative GitOps Lifecycle: All cluster configurations, models, and ingress routes version-controlled in GitHub and continuously synced by Argo CD into Kubernetes.
Zero Inbound Attack Surface: External access managed through Cloudflare Portal DNS and in-cluster Cloudflared Tunnel without opening inbound firewall ports or exposing public IPs.
Cloud-Native Ingress Routing: Traefik routes domain traffic internally with automated TLS termination and dynamic service discovery.
Encapsulated Kubernetes Cluster Mesh: All inference pods, gateways, telemetry agents, dashboards, and databases run as native child workloads under the Kubernetes container parent.
Zero Data Leakage: Complete control over inference workloads with in-cluster model execution hosted on Kubernetes.
Unified LiteLLM Proxying: Standardized OpenAI-compatible API interface with key budgeting, rate limiting, and automated Langfuse callbacks.
Multi-Plane Observability: Headlamp for Kubernetes cluster operations, Langfuse for LLM traces/token analytics, and Netdata for per-second CPU/GPU/memory hardware diagnostics.

keyMetrics.resilienceTier: High-Availability K8s Deployment with Auto-Restart & GitOps Self-Healing

data.label: Cloudflared Tunnel Daemon
data.subtitle: Zero Trust Ingress Agent
data.description: Child Kubernetes Deployment in namespace 'cloudflare'. Runs the lightweight Cloudflare Tunnel daemon (`cloudflared`), creating secure outbound-only encrypted QUIC/HTTP2 tunnels to Cloudflare Edge without exposing public IP addresses or opening inbound firewall ports.
responsibilities: Maintains persistent outbound encrypted QUIC/HTTP2 tunnels to Cloudflare global edge
Securely delivers incoming internet traffic directly to the in-cluster Traefik Ingress Controller
Eliminates public IP requirements and closes all inbound firewall ports
Handles automatic connection health checks and seamless tunnel reconnection
failureModes: Tunnel token invalidation or secret configuration drift
Temporary egress network disruption causing tunnel reconnection delay

configSnippet.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cloudflared
  namespace: cloudflare
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cloudflared
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cloudflared
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cloudflared
        image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
        args: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run", "--token", "$(TUNNEL_TOKEN)"]
        env:
        - name: TUNNEL_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: cloudflare-tunnel-token
              key: token

tradeoffs.decision: Zero Trust Ingress (Cloudflare Tunnels + Traefik) vs Public Cloud Load Balancer / NodePort
tradeoffs.chosenApproach: Cloudflare Tunnel daemon (cloudflared) inside cluster bridging to Traefik Ingress Controller
pros: Eliminates public IP requirements and closes all inbound firewall ports (Zero Inbound Attack Surface)
Automated DDoS mitigation, edge caching, and WAF inspection through Cloudflare Edge
Traefik provides cloud-native HTTP/HTTPS routing, middleware, and dynamic pod discovery
Zero recurring cloud load balancer costs ($18-25/mo saved per LB)
cons: Requires maintaining cloudflared agent and Traefik IngressRoute CRDs in GitOps
Traffic depends on outbound internet connectivity to Cloudflare Anycast edge
rejectedAlternatives: Exposing NodePorts directly to the public internet (severe security vulnerability)
Provisioning individual public cloud LoadBalancers per service (expensive and complex firewall management)

tradeoffs.decision: Cluster Management UI (Headlamp) vs Raw Kubectl CLI Only
tradeoffs.chosenApproach: Headlamp Kubernetes web dashboard deployed in-cluster with RBAC control
pros: Intuitive visual overview of namespaces, pods, logs, and GPU resource limits for dev teams
Plugin ecosystem for custom CRDs and cluster health widgets at headlamp.plotkai.in
Enforces native Kubernetes ServiceAccount RBAC permissions without shared kubeconfigs
cons: Requires secure ingress routing and authentication protection
rejectedAlternatives: Vanilla Kubernetes Dashboard (higher maintenance overhead, dated UI)
Distributing raw admin kubeconfig files to all team members (dangerous privilege escalation risk)

tradeoffs.decision: GitOps Continuous Delivery (Argo CD + GitHub) vs Manual Kubectl / Helm Apply
tradeoffs.chosenApproach: Argo CD GitOps controller synchronizing from GitHub repository into Kubernetes
pros: Eliminates manual kubectl errors and configuration drift across cluster environments
Audit trail of every manifest change stored immutably in Git commits
Automated self-healing reverts accidental or malicious unapproved cluster mutations
Visual rollout status, health checks, and one-click rollbacks via Argo CD UI
cons: Requires learning GitOps concepts and maintaining Argo CD controller instances
Minor propagation delay (~10-30s) when waiting for webhook/sync cycle
rejectedAlternatives: Direct manual `kubectl apply` from local developer machine (lacks version control, high risk of drift)
Ad-hoc shell scripts running in CI without reconciliation controller

tradeoffs.chosenApproach: LiteLLM Proxy deployed as a centralized K8s service
pros: Provides OpenAI-compatible API interface for seamless client compatibility
Native plug-and-play callbacks for Langfuse without altering client apps
Centralized virtual key generation, rate limiting, and team budgeting
cons: Adds an additional hop (approx. 4-5ms) in the network path
Requires maintaining a PostgreSQL database for stateful key storage
rejectedAlternatives: Connecting NextChat directly to the raw vLLM pod (lacks rate limits and observability hooks)
Custom reverse proxy written from scratch (high maintenance overhead)

tradeoffs.chosenApproach: Triple-plane architecture: Headlamp for K8s operations + Langfuse for LLM traces + Netdata for real-time infrastructure
pros: Headlamp provides visual cluster management, pod logs, and workload statuses
Langfuse captures prompt semantics, token usage, latency percentiles, and evaluations
Netdata provides sub-second live hardware telemetry (VRAM, CPU, I/O) without sign-in friction
Decoupled operational layers allow debugging application vs infrastructure issues independently
cons: Three specialized web dashboards for cluster, LLM trace, and telemetry operations

securityAndCompliance.area: Zero Inbound Attack Surface & Perimeter Defense
securityAndCompliance.standard: Cloudflare Zero Trust Tunnel & Anycast WAF
securityAndCompliance.implementation: All inbound traffic enters via Cloudflare Portal DNS and in-cluster Cloudflared Tunnels. No public cluster IP addresses or inbound firewall ports (80/443) are exposed to the internet.
Headlamp dashboard operations are bounded by Kubernetes ServiceAccount RBAC policies, preventing unauthorized cluster escalation or namespace modifications.
All deployment definitions are stored in GitHub with protected branch rules, required pull request reviews, and GPG commit signature validation before Argo CD reconciles changes.
All user prompts and generated model tokens remain strictly confined within the Kubernetes cluster private network. No external API calls are made.
LiteLLM enforces hashed virtual API keys with granular token budgets, expiration timestamps, and per-user rate limits.

All public ingress endpoints (chat.plotkai.in, gateway.plotkai.in, langfuse.plotkai.in, netdata.plotkai.in, headlamp.plotkai.in, argocd.plotkai.in) are secured via cert-manager and Traefik Let's Encrypt TLS certificates.
LiteLLM and Langfuse dashboards enforce authenticated credentials (tester@plotkai.in / Tester@123456), while Netdata provides read-only telemetry exploration.
